title: Memdb serialization, deserialization, and store replacement

scope.rationale: These three source functions resolve a schema to a private memdb store, expose copied or borrowed database images, and replace a schema store with caller-provided bytes and ownership/resize/read-only flags. Native public APIs preserve main-schema copy/NOCOPY sizing and stage replacement buffers with source-shaped capacity, configured maximum, resize, ownership, and read-only flags before retiring the existing database; attached-schema closure and complete differential assurance remain open.
excluded_responsibilities: Memdb file methods and delegated VFS services assigned to memdb-file-storage-locking-and-mapping
Attached schema catalog behavior outside currently supported main schema

external_source_responsibilities: Public API connection mutex and full Btree/Pager page-by-page fallback
dependencies.caller_closure: Public sqlite3_serialize/sqlite3_deserialize and backup APIs route through production Connection memory or Unix backend. Main-schema copy, NOCOPY borrow, replacement reopen, read-only mode, and FREEONCLOSE cleanup are reachable.

inputs: Connection, nullable/default schema, nullable size output, image pointer, database size, buffer capacity and ownership flags
outputs: Copied sqlite3_malloc image, borrowed private-memdb pointer, null with size, or exact result code
contracts.ownership: Copy serialization returns process-manager memory to caller. NOCOPY borrows store bytes. Deserialization transfers or borrows pData according to FREEONCLOSE and publishes no partial replacement on failure.
contracts.state_and_results: Size output begins at -1, successful schema resolution reports image size, NOCOPY succeeds only for private memdb, and deserialize sets size/capacity/max/flags before reopening schema.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Source holds connection then MemStore mutexes. Native serialized connection path uses MemoryVfs registry/store mutexes and may read Unix file bytes; no callbacks.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Invalid connection/sizes return misuse, missing schema returns null/error, OOM returns null/NOMEM. Failure before replacement publication preserves the existing usable database, and every failure honors FREEONCLOSE exactly without double-free.

representation_differences: Private main-memory database lookup uses Connection.memory_backend instead of sqlite3_file_control plus memdb_io_methods identity.
NOCOPY now borrows the exact native main-store byte pointer and copied output uses the process memory manager.

Deserialize stages pData directly as native store bytes, retains the exact allocator-manager domain for realloc/free, preserves szDb/szBuf, applies max(szBuf, configured process memdb maximum), doubles reallocations up to that bound, and keeps post-replacement NOCOPY pointer identity.
Only main schema is supported; source can replace eligible attached schemas.

oracle.protocol: Native SQL frontend and C ABI integration create a database image, copy serialize with nullable size, NOCOPY borrow with exact native pointer/size, reject missing schema with size -1, deserialize a clone, enforce read-only opening, validate negative-capacity armor, preserve the old database on pre-publication allocation failure, release FREEONCLOSE input, enforce the configured maximum, and inject realloc failure while checking exact pointer/content/size continuation. A pinned C/Zig flag/ownership differential remains open.
oracle.normalization: Database image bytes, sizes, result codes and within-worker pointer identity are exact. Absolute C/Zig addresses are not compared.

assurance.oom: Copy allocation, direct FREEONCLOSE close, borrowed storage, read-only storage, successful resize, configured maximum, pre-publication backend OOM, exact NOMEM, old-database continuation, input release, and injected allocator-manager realloc failure with unchanged pointer/content/size are covered for main schema. Attached-schema ownership remains open.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: Unix serialization reads a stable file in the serialized connection path. Exact connection/store lock ordering and concurrent API misuse traces remain open.
assurance.malformed_input: Negative size/capacity, null data and unknown schema have native guards; full source API-armor matrix remains open.
assurance.continuation: Successful clone and subsequent SQL pass. Pre-publication allocation failure preserves queryable old content and releases FREEONCLOSE input; post-publication malformed/reopen continuation remains open.
assurance.performance: NOCOPY is constant time. Copy serialization is linear; disk path reads one image rather than source page iteration.

integration.native_call_path: C ABI sqlite3_serialize/sqlite3_deserialize -> Connection memory/Unix backend -> MemoryVfs/Pager reopen
integration.bounded_owner_retired: No separate test-only image owner; backup API uses these production exports.

independent_review.notes: Requires attached-schema replacement, post-publication malformed continuation, complete cross-schema differential, assurance, and independent review.

known_blockers: Support eligible attached schemas and the source reopen path, then extend the main-schema ownership/OOM matrix across schemas.
Add pinned C/Zig flags, OOM, ownership and continuation differential.

implementation_spans: upstream/sqlite/src/memdb.c was reviewed completely, with lines 734-745 covering schema/file-control resolution and private-store rejection of shared names

Lines 750-837 were reviewed completely for API armor/mutex, size initialization, private memdb fast path, NOCOPY/copy ownership, ordinary Btree page-count and page-by-page fallback, empty-database materialization, and cleanup

Lines 841-910 were reviewed completely for deserialize armor, schema constraints, ATTACH/reopen flow, private-store resolution, caller-buffer transfer, size/capacity/max/flags publication, FREEONCLOSE failure cleanup and mutex exit

src/core/memdb.zig schema resolution/serialize/deserialize owner, vfs.zig external-buffer adoption/growth/free, and sql_frontend.zig public exports/tests/backup callers were reviewed; mapped targets are AST-hashed
callers: Public sqlite3_serialize/sqlite3_deserialize exports and backup clone flow call this unit under the serialized connection path
Main-schema memory databases use private MemoryVfs images; named shared memdb denies NOCOPY; Unix serialization uses a native whole-file fallback rather than source page iteration
Deserialize closes/replaces the existing main database, adopts caller storage, reopens Pager/Btree against the replacement, and later close frees storage only with FREEONCLOSE
callees: memdbFromDbSchema resolves through file control, verifies memdb methods, locks store, and returns only private zFName-null stores

Serialize initializes piSize to -1 after mutex entry, resolves schema, reports private-store size, borrows exact bytes for NOCOPY or sqlite3_malloc-copies them; ordinary Btree path obtains page count/page size and copies each page, zero-filling failed page gets

Deserialize rejects invalid handle/negative sizes, restricts temp schema, prepares ATTACH with reopenMemdb, resolves the new private store, transfers pData exactly once, publishes sz/szAlloc/szMax=max(buffer,global maximum)/flags, and frees untransferred FREEONCLOSE input on every failure

Native adoption records external pointer, logical size, capacity, resize/readonly/free flags; growth reallocates through process manager with source doubling/maximum and preserves pointer/content on failure
assertions_branches_cleanup: All 44 behavior IDs cover schema resolution, size initialization, private/shared/ordinary branches, NOCOPY, empty database materialization, allocation/page loop cleanup, deserialize armor/schema/reopen, transfer and failure FREEONCLOSE

Copy results are caller-owned sqlite3_malloc memory; NOCOPY is borrowed and only available for private stores; adopted bytes are borrowed or owned according to FREEONCLOSE and must not be double-freed

Native main-schema copy/NOCOPY/adoption/readonly/resizable paths, configured maximum, pre-publication OOM continuation, and exact realloc-failure pointer/content/size preservation are reachable and tested, but attached-schema reopen, exact Btree page-by-page fallback equivalence, and post-publication malformed continuation remain blockers
Failure before transfer honors FREEONCLOSE; failure after successful transfer leaves the replacement backend as owner and connection closable, though complete source continuation traces remain open
upstream_tests: upstream memdb1.test covers main/attached serialization, direct/readonly/maxsize/empty/malformed deserialize, misuse, replacement restrictions, reopen and continuation; memdb.test/memdb2.test and corruption/fuzz suites exercise consumed images

Project SQL integration verifies nullable size, copy ownership, exact NOCOPY pointer/size, missing schema size -1, negative-capacity armor, clone SQL, direct adopted-pointer identity, resizable growth, FREEONCLOSE, readonly reopen/write rejection and close; VFS injection verifies realloc OOM leaves the original manager allocation, content, and logical size unchanged
Backup integration routes through the same public exports, establishing a production caller; focused memdb tests cover byte-store size/limit/growth owners
A pinned C/Zig flag/ownership/OOM differential, attached schemas, and full transferred-buffer failure continuation remain explicit blockers rather than claimed assurance
